author: Inside Edition
description: Activist Dolores Huerta has died. Her family made the announcement on her foundation's social media channels. Huerta spent her life championing labor rights. She co-founded the United Farmworkers of America in 1966 with Cesar Chavez. The organization, which still exists, fought for better working conditions for farm laborers, and the right to unionize. Dolores Huerta was 96.
title: Labor Rights Activist Dolores Huerta Dies At 96

author: Inside Edition
description: A New York man, worried about speeding cars on his street, took matters into his own hands by installing speedbumps. Boris Macias of Brooklyn tells WCBS that for about a week, his DIY project forced drivers to slow down or experience jarring bumps. The homemade speedbumps didn't get every car to slow down, but he said he hoped drivers got the message to be more careful. The city's Department of Transportation has since removed them. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Brooklyn Man Installs Speedbumps To Make His Street Safer

author: Inside Edition
description: Little Isabella gave her mom a great big hug when she appeared at her North Carolina elementary school.
title: Air Force Mom Surprises Daughter At School In Heartwarming Homecoming #shorts

author: Inside Edition
description: Another cold case has been linked to serial killer Ted Bundy. Officials in Summit County, Utah, say DNA from the case of Melissa Ann Smith, who was found dead in 1974, was a match to the DNA profile on file in Florida for Bundy. Utah investigators say they already had Bundy's DNA information because earlier this year they were able to link it to the cold case murder of Laura Amy in a different county. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Utah Investigators Link 1974 Cold Case Murder To Serial Killer Ted Bundy
